title: An AI health claim meets the advertising rules

chunks.title: Draft app-store text promises results
chunks.release_note: Marketing wants to publish a claim next week and to name the partner clinic.

question.coach: May this text be published as it stands?
question.clinic: May the clinic be named in this text, and what must it do first?
question.default: What do the rules say about this step?

coach: Draft app-store text from the Miqyas marketing page: 'Our AI coach reverses prediabetes in 30 days. Guaranteed results, no side effects.' It is due to be published next week.
clinic: The partner clinic was asked to be named in the same text as 'clinically supervised by our doctors'. The clinic has not seen the final wording.

incomplete: Whether the text has gone through any advertising approval.
policy_questions: prior approval is required before publishing a health advertisement
prohibited expressions in health advertisements such as guaranteed results and no side effects

chunks.title: A paid influencer posts a before-and-after story
chunks.release_note: An influencer shared a user's blood-sugar story; the media desk got a complaint.

question.coach: What must Miqyas do about the post and the numbers it supplied?
question.authority: Does the complaint on file require any action about Miqyas?
question.default: What do the rules say about this step?

coach: A paid influencer posted a before-and-after story about a Miqyas user's blood sugar. Miqyas has no record that the user agreed to appear. Miqyas had given the influencer the user's anonymised numbers.
authority: The media-regulator desk received one public complaint about the influencer post. The complaint does not name Miqyas.

incomplete: Whether the numbers were truly anonymised, and whether the user can be recognised from the post.
policy_questions: health advertisements by influencers and endorsement of health products and services
use of patient testimonials and before and after results in health advertising

chunks.title: The app starts showing AI-written personalised outcome messages
chunks.release_note: Nobody has decided whether in-app AI messages count as advertising.

question.coach: Do in-app AI messages that name a medical outcome count as advertising?
question.clinic: Do such messages fall under the clinic's advertising approvals?
question.authority: How should automatically generated personalised health messages be treated?
question.default: What do the rules say about this step?

coach: In the app, the coach now shows each user a model-written message such as: 'Based on your data, you have a low chance of developing diabetes. Keep using Miqyas.'
clinic: The clinic's compliance officer asks whether in-app AI messages that name a medical outcome fall under the clinic's advertising approvals.
authority: The regulator desk has no instruction on how to treat automatically generated personalised messages.

incomplete: Whether any text in the knowledge base addresses AI-generated or personalised health messages.
policy_questions: AI generated or automated personalised health messages in health advertising
health claims by AI systems must be accurate and not misleading
